text:
Registered residential sales totaled 10,419 units valued at AED 27,337,275,204 over the last four weeks, representing a 4.4 percent decrease in volume compared to the previous four weeks. Mortgage registrations stood at 3,889, which are tracked separately from sales transactions. The off-plan share of sales was 65.4 percent, down from 67.2 percent in the prior period.

The median residential price per square foot declined to AED 1,677, a 1.9 percent drop from the previous four-week median of AED 1,709. Top performing areas by sales volume include Dubai South with 4,608 sales and Down Town Jabal Ali with 2,517 sales. In Dubai South, the median price per square foot was AED 1,705.1, while Down Town Jabal Ali recorded AED 1,732.3. Business Bay showed a median of AED 2,100.5 per square foot, reflecting a significant 8.2 percent decrease over the last twelve weeks.

Rental activity recorded 81,116 contracts with a renewal share of 50.5 percent. The median residential rent was AED 70,900 per year. Estimated gross yields were highest in International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent for flats, followed by Town Square at 7.0 percent. Dubai Sports City and Dubai Studio City both recorded 6.5 percent yields, while Dubai Production City reached 6.4 percent.

Areas showing price heating include Al Yufrah 1 with a 35.9 percent increase and Damac Hills with a 16.6 percent rise. Cooling areas include Palm Deira at minus 18.1 percent and Wadi Al Safa 7 at minus 14.1 percent. An anomaly monitor flagged 1,000 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
